## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Solids
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Solids — parametric surfaces for the solids
//  - The typed polyhedral solids as polygon meshes
//  - Deformation bodies for the profile-generated solids

library Solids
{
    //==
    // # Solids — parametric surfaces for the solids
    //
    // The parametric boundary surface of each solid, as the IParametricSurface
    // obligations. Solids are centered at the origin with Z as the up axis in their
    // local frame; UV is in [0,1]x[0,1]: U wraps around the Z axis (ClosedU is true
    // for every solid), V runs up the shape (or around it, for the torus). Polygonal
    // solids walk their profile at constant rate with flat sides (linear between
    // vertices), so a UV quad grid meshes them exactly.
    //
    // Every solid carries its own placement, so the local-frame convention above
    // describes the solid's LOCAL frame and the local point is mapped to world at
    // the end of each body — through the type's own `Frame` where it has one,
    // through its `Orientation` quaternion where it has one, and otherwise through
    // `AxisFrame`, which manufactures a stable (but arbitrary) frame around a
    // `Center`/`Axis` pair. The UV seam therefore lands at an arbitrary azimuth for
    // the Center/Axis solids, which is all a seam needs; nothing downstream may
    // assume where it is.
    //
    // Because U always wraps and V (except the torus) does not, the matching face
    // grid is `AllQuadFaceIndices(nCols, nRows, true, false)` from
    // `meshes.library.plato` — the "flat sides, constant rate" clause is what
    // makes that grid mesh the polygonal solids EXACTLY rather than approximately.

    //==
    // Shared profile helpers

    // The point at `radius` from the origin in direction `a`, in the XY plane.
    PointOnCircle(a: Angle, radius: Number): Point2D
        => (a.Cos * radius, a.Sin * radius);

    // The point at angle `a` on the unit circle centered at the origin.
    // Local helper: the point at angle `a` on the unit circle centered at the origin.
    // Defined here so this library is self-contained; if `curves-shapes.types.plato`
    // later grows a canonical unit-circle evaluator, prefer that and delete this.
    PointOnUnitCircle(a: Angle): Point2D
        => PointOnCircle(a, 1.0);

    // A point on the regular n-gon inscribed in the unit circle, walked at
    // CONSTANT RATE: t in [0,1] covers the whole perimeter and the path is linear
    // between vertices (so the sides are genuinely flat, not chorded arcs). t is
    // taken modulo 1, so the walk repeats. Precondition: n >= 3.
    NGonPoint(t: Number, n: Integer): Point2D
    {
        var sides = n.ToNumber;
        var p = (t - t.Floor) * sides;
        var f = p - p.Floor;
        var a = PointOnUnitCircle((p.Floor / sides).Turns);
        var b = PointOnUnitCircle(((p.Floor + 1.0) / sides).Turns);
        return a.Lerp(b, f);
    }

    // A point on the axis-aligned square with corners at (+-1, +-1), walked at
    // constant rate: a 4-gon rotated an eighth turn and scaled by sqrt(2) so its
    // sides — not its vertices — land on the axes.
    SquarePoint(t: Number): Point2D
    {
        var c = (2.0).Sqrt;
        var p = (t - t.Floor) * 4.0;
        var f = p - p.Floor;
        var a = PointOnCircle(((p.Floor + 0.5) / 4.0).Turns, c);
        var b = PointOnCircle(((p.Floor + 1.5) / 4.0).Turns, c);
        return a.Lerp(b, f);
    }

    // The latitude/longitude point on the unit sphere: U wraps around the equator,
    // V runs from the north pole (V = 0) to the south pole (V = 1).
    UnitSpherePoint(uv: UvCoordinate): Vector3D
    {
        var theta = uv.U.Turns;
        var phi = (uv.V * 0.5).Turns;
        return (phi.Sin * theta.Cos, phi.Sin * theta.Sin, phi.Cos);
    }

    // A frame-local point mapped to world coordinates: the frame origin displaced
    // along its own axes by the local coordinates.
    PointInFrame(f: Frame3D, local: Point3D): Point3D
        => (f.Origin.X + f.XAxis.Vector.X * local.X + f.YAxis.Vector.X * local.Y + f.ZAxis.Vector.X * local.Z,
            f.Origin.Y + f.XAxis.Vector.Y * local.X + f.YAxis.Vector.Y * local.Y + f.ZAxis.Vector.Y * local.Z,
            f.Origin.Z + f.XAxis.Vector.Z * local.X + f.YAxis.Vector.Z * local.Y + f.ZAxis.Vector.Z * local.Z);

    // A right-handed orthonormal frame at `center` whose Z axis is `axis`. The X
    // axis is chosen by crossing `axis` with whichever world axis it is least
    // aligned with, so the construction never degenerates; the resulting azimuth
    // is arbitrary but stable, which is all a UV seam requires.
    AxisFrame(center: Point3D, axis: Direction3D): Frame3D
    {
        var z = axis.Vector;
        var helper = z.Z.Abs < 0.9 ? Vector3D.UnitZ : Vector3D.UnitX;
        var x = helper.Cross(z).Normalize;
        var y = z.Cross(x);
        return (center, Direction3D(x), Direction3D(y), Direction3D(z));
    }

    //==
    // Surfaces of revolution

    // U wraps the equator, V runs pole to pole.
    Eval(s: Sphere, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D
    {
        var d = UnitSpherePoint(uv);
        return (s.Center.X + d.X * s.Radius,
                s.Center.Y + d.Y * s.Radius,
                s.Center.Z + d.Z * s.Radius);
    }
    ClosedU(s: Sphere): Boolean => true;
    ClosedV(s: Sphere): Boolean => false;

    // The unit sphere scaled by the semi-axes, then rotated by Orientation.
    Eval(s: Ellipsoid, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D
    {
        var d = UnitSpherePoint(uv);
        var local = Vector3D(d.X * s.SemiAxes.X, d.Y * s.SemiAxes.Y, d.Z * s.SemiAxes.Z);
        var w = local.Transform(s.Orientation);
        return (s.Center.X + w.X, s.Center.Y + w.Y, s.Center.Z + w.Z);
    }
    ClosedU(s: Ellipsoid): Boolean => true;
    ClosedV(s: Ellipsoid): Boolean => false;

    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torus#Geometry: U goes around the main (Axis)
    // circle, V around the tube — so a torus is the one solid closed in BOTH.
    Eval(s: Torus, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D
    {
        var f = AxisFrame(s.Center, s.Axis);
        var u = uv.U.Turns;
        var v = uv.V.Turns;
        var ring = s.MajorRadius + s.MinorRadius * v.Cos;
        return f.PointInFrame(Point3D(ring * u.Cos, ring * u.Sin, s.MinorRadius * v.Sin));
    }
    ClosedU(s: Torus): Boolean => true;
    ClosedV(s: Torus): Boolean => true;

    // The lateral wall only (the flat caps are not part of the UV rectangle):
    // V = 0 is the -Height/2 rim, V = 1 the +Height/2 rim.
    Eval(s: Cylinder, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D
    {
        var f = AxisFrame(s.Center, s.Axis);
        var p = PointOnCircle(uv.U.Turns, s.Radius);
        return f.PointInFrame(Point3D(p.X, p.Y, (uv.V - 0.5) * s.Height));
    }
    ClosedU(s: Cylinder): Boolean => true;
    ClosedV(s: Cylinder): Boolean => false;
```
